scope.comparison: Every delta gate compares the promotion candidate (scorer allowed to set Confidence and action) with the legacy result of the same frozen corpus under the deterministic path (scorer shadow-only). delta = candidate - legacy.

framing.objective: Improve discrimination of ambiguous generic-token candidates (twin discrimination and independent false alarms on the scored specificities).
framing.constraints: Every gate is a hard constraint. A gate cannot be traded against another gate, no gate is weighted, and no F1, accuracy or other combined figure is computed or published.

beta9.statement: Beta.9 ships the scorer shadow-only. It needs no passing answer to question 5, and a failing or unevaluated answer to questions 1-4 does not block it: the beta.9 qualification record (#282) records whatever answers exist. No outcome of this contract changes beta.9 detection, Confidence, action or findings.

public: aggregate rates and counts per stratum with at least 5 rows
never: fitted weights, caps or band cut-offs

identity.rule: All evidence cited by one promotion decision carries the same identity tuple. A promotion candidate has a model fingerprint and a candidate artifact hash that no shadow-only candidate carried (redact-secret#798). Evidence keyed to another tuple is stale and is regenerated, never carried over.

questions.question: Is the research scorer mathematically coherent and calibrated for its stated population?
questions.population: the development population the calibration run states (#255); a calibrated estimate is valid for that population only

questions.question: Does it improve the targeted ambiguous population?
questions.population: generic-token candidates of the scored specificities in the evaluation-only sources of the active tuning manifest

questions.question: Does it preserve security outcomes elsewhere?
questions.population: every evaluation-only source of the active tuning manifest: regression categories, development-evaluation categories and accepted adversarial packs, all families

questions.question: Does it resist deliberate score-evasion and negative-evidence abuse?
questions.population: the #289 deterministic mutation variants, reported through the score-evasion aggregate

questions.question: What independent evidence is required before a later release could enable enforcement?
questions.population: the protected holdout, the custodian blind evaluation, and product-supplied runtime, performance and size qualification of the exact promotion candidate

gates.question: Q1
gates.rationale: Every positive group cap is below the high cut-off, randomness plus lexical cannot reach high, the cut-offs strictly increase, and the artifact drift check is clean (product ADR sections 3 and 10).

gates.question: Q1
gates.rationale: The section 4 property tests pass for the exact artifact revision; a non-monotone artifact is invalid whatever its benchmark results.

gates.question: Q1
gates.rationale: On the stated population the observed share of must-redact rows does not decrease from band none to band high, overall and in every family stratum with enough rows.

gates.question: Q1
gates.rationale: The benchmark-side calibrated estimate for the stated development population has expected calibration error at most 0.05. The value stays maintainer-local; only the verdict is public.

gates.question: Q1
gates.rationale: Reweighting authored rows to half the weight selects the same configuration (calibration experiments section 7), so the choice is not an artefact of generated rows.

gates.question: Q2
gates.rationale: The objective. Promotion is worth its risk only if it discriminates one-property twins at least 5 points better than the legacy path, and no stratum discriminates worse.

gates.question: Q2
gates.rationale: On the targeted population the promoted path raises no more independent controls than the legacy path, overall or in any stratum.

gates.question: Q2
gates.rationale: An improvement measured on a minority of rows is not an improvement. Unresolved rows (companion spans, truncated values) count against the share.

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: Zero tolerance: no must-redact span that the legacy path redacts is leaked by the promoted path, in any stratum.

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: The leaked-span rate, must-redact and policy spans reported separately, does not rise overall or in any stratum.

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: No aggregate false-alarm increase. A single stratum may rise by at most one point, so one extra alarm in a large stratum is visible without blocking; the aggregate bound still holds.

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: Bytes of flagged controls per must-redact byte do not rise overall, and rise by at most 0.01 in any stratum.

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: A private-key, provider or structural candidate never changes Confidence, range, type or action under the promoted path (product ADR section 5).

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: No emitted candidate is removed or narrowed by statistical evidence. Relaxing this needs a new product decision and a new contract version, and can never apply to the invariant specificities.

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: Every regression fixture the legacy path passes still passes; regression categories are evaluation-only, so this cannot be met by fitting to them.

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: A promoted outcome that differs between replays, runtimes or whole-input and incremental paths is not qualified.

gates.question: Q3
gates.rationale: Every fixture whose outcome the promotion changes, in either direction, carries a review-ledger decision before the gate is read.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: The aggregate was produced in promotion-candidate mode against the exact promotion identity; a beta.9 shadow-mode aggregate cannot answer Q4 for a promotion.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: Every required attack class is reported with at least minimumVariantsPerClass resolved variants.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: Invariant specificities are never weakened, negative evidence needs a full grammar match, and no statistical signal turns a deterministic positive into a non-finding, for every variant.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: Zero tolerance: no mutation variant leaks under the promoted path that the legacy path redacts. Promotion never opens a bypass the deterministic path closes.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: The share of variants that keep their expected detection is no lower than the legacy path's, overall and per attack class.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: Negative evidence never applies to a variant that only partly matches an exclusion grammar (product ADR section 6).

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: Mutated controls (negative-evidence mixtures and lookalikes) are not flagged more often than under the legacy path.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: Collateral on mutation variants does not rise.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: No variant has an outcome that differs between replays.

gates.question: Q4
gates.rationale: At most 5% of variants may be unresolved; unresolved variants are counted, never dropped.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: The promotion candidate carries a model fingerprint that no shadow-only artifact revision carried.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: The promotion candidate is a new frozen candidate (new candidate artifact hash); shadow-only candidates are never promoted in place.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: Every cited piece of evidence carries the promotion candidate's identity tuple and none is stale.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: The product ADR requires a new decision before statistical evidence may change Confidence or action; that decision is accepted in the product repository.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: A complete, custodian-declared protected-holdout run of the exact promotion candidate, in a sealed epoch that is not contaminated, within its budget, after the tuning manifest was frozen with holdoutAccess none.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: On the protected holdout the leaked-span rate does not rise, overall or in any kind:tier stratum, relative to the reference run in the same epoch.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: On the protected holdout the false-alarm rate does not rise relative to the reference run in the same epoch.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: The Q2 improvement holds its direction on data the tuning never saw.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: The holdout result is measured on at least 90% of its cases.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: The custodian-controlled blind evaluation of the exact promotion candidate is complete and states what independence it achieved.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: Native Rust, the Node addon, WebAssembly and Python produce identical evidence and Confidence outcomes.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: Whole-input and incremental scans produce identical outcomes.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: Maximum-length contextual candidates and repeated or periodic worst cases stay within the performance acceptance criteria, with no runtime model file or network dependency.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: The #143 budget report for the promotion candidate against the last released baseline is within budget or a recorded tradeoff for latency, initialization and memory; regression, invalid-measurement and not-evaluated all fail.

gates.question: Q5
gates.rationale: WebAssembly, bundle, npm, addon, wheel and CLI sizes of the promotion candidate are within the #143 size budget or a recorded tradeoff (the #772 raw, gzip and brotli deltas feed it).
